item.title: 1920s Alphington home heads to auction for $3.4 million
item.description: An Arts and Crafts home located at 49 Lucerne Crescent, Alphington, is scheduled for auction soon. The home, built in 1920, features unique handcrafted details like Kookaburra stained-glass windows and modern upgrades. Recent renovations have preserved its character and enhanced livability, including adding en suites and a home office. The property boasts a landscaped garden with various plants and outdoor family amenities, such as a pool and spa.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Antarctic sea ice reached its third-lowest winter maximum in satellite records
item.description: On September 14, Antarctic sea ice reached its peak extent, covering around 17.59 million square kilometres. However, this year marks the third lowest maximum on record, indicating a concerning trend as it falls below the long-term average. The past four winters have each presented historically low sea ice levels, raising urgent questions about future climate impacts driven by this alarming decline in coverage.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2010, Moby bought Hollywood’s Wolf’s Lair for $3.925 M, restored it and sold it for $12.4 M
item.description: In 2010, musician Moby bought Wolf’s Lair, a castle-like estate built in 1927 in the Hollywood Hills, for $3.925 million. He restored the 3.3-acre property while preserving its original character and period details. Four years later, he sold the estate for $12.4 million, approximately $8.475 million more than his original purchase price.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 17-year-old Iris Shen uses clams to test blood-cancer drugs, wins $150,000 prize
item.description: Iris Shen, a bright high school student hailing from The Woodlands, Texas, gained acclaim for her groundbreaking research on cancer. She explored a novel drug’s effects on clams to study its impact on blood cancer. The results of her experiment suggest new avenues for drug discovery, underlining the need for innovative approaches in medical research. This recognition underscores the crucial role of young scientists in furthering our scientific knowledge.

item.title: Scientists discover a bamboo coral forest nearly 1,400 metres below the surface
item.description: Researchers located a previously unknown deep-water bamboo coral forest during an expedition near the Xisha Islands. The coral forest, recorded at depths of 1,200 to 1,380 metres, features various marine species and habitats. Observations showed increased coral density as depth decreased, highlighting its ecological significance. Active currents and nutrient-rich underwater conditions contribute to the forest's growth and biodiversity.

item.title: Michael Dell-backed firm’s $875 million Boca Raton resort bet draws luxury homebuyers; 40% of first 75 condos claimed
item.description: An impressive $875 million investment is set to transform The Boca Raton resort into a luxurious haven of residential condominiums. With around 40% of these high-end residences already reserved, pricing starts at $8.95 million and can exceed $20 million. This revitalization forms part of the resort's centennial celebrations scheduled for 2026, with construction commencing the same year and concluding by 2029.
item.dc:creator: TOI Tech Desk

item.title: New Yorkers queue for hours to buy subway memorabilia, with signs costing over $1,000
item.description: New Yorkers queued for hours at an annual MTA sale in south Brooklyn to buy discarded subway signs, seats and MetroCards. Station signs cost $500 to over $1,000, while orange subway seats sold for around $900. Filmmaker Spike Lee was among the shoppers, purchasing a Penn Station sign. The two-day event attracts around 4,000 visitors annually.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Opal Tower cracks forced Christmas Eve evacuation in 2018; eight years later, it is defect-free
item.description: After nearly eight years of uncertainty, Sydney's Opal Tower has officially been declared defect-free, following significant structural issues uncovered in December 2018. This crisis led to evacuations, extensive repairs, and legal conflicts regarding the building's safety standards. Most residents have safely returned after comprehensive rectification processes, and property owners will receive compensation along with a 20-year structural warranty.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 14-year-old Indonesian plants 38,000 mangroves, helps local women turn them into sustainable products
item.description: In Indonesia, young activist Harley Fatahillah Yodhaloka Sunoto is leading a passionate campaign for mangrove restoration and climate education. Through his Mangrove Warrior initiative, he has successfully planted thousands of seedlings in critical coastal regions, strengthening ecosystems and supporting local communities. By collaborating with mothers and organizations, Harley is educating on sustainable practices, with an ambitious goal of planting one million mangroves and launching educational programs nationwide.

item.title: How a $5 million donation from Ralph Lauren helped transform cancer care in New York's Harlem
item.description: In 2000, Ralph Lauren's company announced a $5 million donation to establish a cancer care centre in Harlem, New York. Opened in 2003, the centre provided cancer screenings, treatment and patient support to underserved communities. The initiative later expanded, with the Ralph Lauren Corporate Foundation pledging another $25 million in 2022 to improve access to cancer care.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘The Fault in Our Stars’ author John Green helped fund a maternity centre in Sierra Leone; 13 babies born in first 24 hours
item.description: A new maternity centre named the Paul E. Farmer Maternal Center of Excellence opened in Sierra Leone. This facility was built to improve access to maternal and newborn healthcare in the region. On its first day, it received 27 patients and facilitated the birth of 13 babies. The centre aims to reduce maternal mortality and strengthen the local health system through improved standards of care.
